subject: Post-call: Ops/observability evaluation + hyperscaler comparison — next tests & scope
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@dataforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Ops/observability evaluation + hyperscaler comparison — next tests & scope

Sanjay — thanks for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to an agreed POC/test plan. TL;DR: DataForge wants to validate observability, tracing fidelity, and cost/latency tradeoffs vs hyperscaler endpoints before committing to a dedicated contract. You confirmed priority order: 1) accurate tracing & token-level cost attribution, 2) latency tail percentiles (p95/p99) for streaming responses, 3) predictable throughput under bursty workloads.

Summary of what we covered:
- Scope: Core inference (text generation + streaming) + observability surface (per-request tokens, latency breakdown, trace spans across batching/worker hops).
- Hyperscalers you’re testing in parallel: AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI (you mentioned internal benchmarks were in-progress).
- Success criteria: Ability to reproduce tracing spans and tie token counts to business feature IDs; p95 <= 220ms for 256-token streaming baseline; cost delta < 20% vs your current conf if we enable our batching/cache suggestions.

Proposed next tests (we can run these inside a 2-week sandbox):
1) Latency matrix: synthetic load (1–50 concurrent rps) across 128/256/512 token responses; record p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm.
2) Tracing fidelity: end-to-end trace from client request → router → worker → model; verify span names, parent ids, and KV cache hits.
3) Streaming correctness + partial tokens: compare behavior when using function-calling & structured output with streaming enabled.
4) Cost & unit economics: side-by-side tokens billed, batching efficiency, and cache hit rate.
5) Failure & fallback: induce model worker fault to verify graceful fallback to lower-tier variant and the observability for that path.

Attachments (initial): redwood_vs_hyperscalers-matrix.xlsx (comparison matrix), observability-test-plan.md (detailed steps). I’ve also included a short security quicksheet for your SecOps.

Ask from you: confirm the test window (we suggested Apr 6–17), provide a security contact we should loop in, and confirm if you need a private VPC deployment for any of the tests.

Next logistics: if you’re good, I’ll spin up a sandbox (hosted) and drop a HubSpot task with the schedule + direct Drive links. I’ll also add Marissa to run the test orchestration and Laura to track procurement items.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Ops/observability evaluation + hyperscaler comparison — next tests & scope

Thanks Dylan — useful recap. Short answers: we’re aligned on priorities. A couple clarifications before we lock dates: we need SOC2 evidence and a basic data residency statement for the hosted sandbox (we’re currently restricted to us-regions for this project). Also, our security lead (Priya) wants a pre-test questionnaire — happy to run the tests once that’s satisfied.

On the test items: the latency targets look reasonable. For the tracing fidelity test, can Redwood provide sample trace exports (Zipkin/Jaeger) and a short example showing how token-level attribution is surfaced in the trace? That’s a gating item for our eng team.

We’re running parallel bench vs Bedrock/Vertex — one ask: can you include cold-start numbers for models with a 1-minute inactivity window? Their internal numbers show bigger variance there.

Dates: Apr 6–17 works as a tentative window. Procurement: I’ll loop procurement once sec is satisfied — cc’ing Priya.

Thanks — Sanjay

- Cold-start measurement: we’ll run 5 independent cold-start cycles with a 60s idle window and report p50/p95. We’ll also include the worker-level logs and span timelines so you can compare to Bedrock/Vertex outputs.
